# `identical-bitwise-operands`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: correctness · Profile: none · Default: warning · Fixes: fix all · Options: none

Reports a bitwise `&`, `|`, or `^` operation whose left-hand and right-hand
operands evaluate to the exact same path.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Bitwise operations with identical operands are idempotent or self-canceling. In
bitwise logic, `x & x` and `x | x` evaluate to `x`, while `x ^ x` always
evaluates to `0`. Repeating identical operands in bitwise expressions almost
always indicates a copy-paste error or typo where two distinct flags, bitmasks,
or variables were intended.

## When it fires

Always. Redundant bitwise operations indicate either dead code or unintended
behavior when testing or combining flags.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
fn mask(flags: u32) u32 {
    return flags & flags;
}
```
